Please review the following manuscript written by my collaborator.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-j0p5cz23/call-f38737f611fd42b2a5b3662277ef6608/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'command -v pdftotext; command -v pdfinfo; command -v pdftoppm; command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for name in ('pypdf', 'pdfplumber', 'fitz', 'PIL'):
    spec=importlib.util.find_spec(name)
    print(name, spec.origin if spec else None)
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
p=Path('tmp/pdfs');p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    text=page.extract_text()
    (p/f'page-{i:02}.txt').write_text(text)
    print(f'PAGE {i}: {len(text)} characters')
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'--- PAGE {i} ---\\n'+(p/f'page-{i:02}.txt').read_text() for i in range(1,len(r.pages)+1)))
print((p/'page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"

strengths: MaskSub is a simple, technically coherent training method: a shared network learns from labels on unmasked inputs and detached predictions on masked inputs. It adds no inference parameters, and token removal makes the auxiliary branch relatively inexpensive. Its practical contribution supports weak acceptance despite limited conceptual novelty.

The central ImageNet results are convincing. Table 1 reports improvements across ViT-S/B/L/H at both training lengths: 0.6–0.7 percentage points at 400 epochs and 0.3–0.5 at 800 epochs. Table A.13 provides repeated-run support, including ViT-B accuracy of 84.08 ± 0.02 versus the reported baseline of 83.46 ± 0.04.

Training-budget comparisons substantiate usefulness beyond simply spending more computation. Table 8 reports ViT-B accuracy of 84.1 at 25 GPU-days versus 83.7 at 26 GPU-days for longer baseline training. Table 9 also shows a favorable comparison with CoSub: 84.1 versus 83.9 accuracy at 25.1 versus 35.3 GPU-days.

Evaluation is unusually broad for a training regularizer, covering pretrained-model finetuning, ResNets, Swin, classification transfer, segmentation, detection, and robustness. Improvements include 0.4–0.6 mIoU on ADE20K and ViT-B ImageNet-A accuracy increasing from 36.8 to 41.9. These results establish relevance beyond the primary classification benchmark.

The appendix supplies useful ablations and implementation details. Table A.6 supports the importance of distillation, Tables A.7–A.8 examine masking ratios and loss weights, and repeated-run experiments strengthen several findings. Algorithm 1, recipe tables B.1–B.2, and the provided code link support reproducibility of the core method.
weaknesses: Methodological novelty is primarily the integration of existing components. Equation (3) is conventional detached-target consistency/self-distillation: cross-entropy H(p,q) and KL(p||q) produce identical student gradients when p is detached. Consequently, the claimed distinction from UDA based on 'distillation loss' versus 'consistency loss' is not technically persuasive. The operational differences and empirical effectiveness are stronger contributions than the loss formulation.

The explanation of automatic difficulty control exceeds the evidence. Figure 2 shows gradient and convergence trends, but does not establish that masking acts exclusively on examples the main branch predicts successfully. There is no correctness gate, and confidently incorrect predictions can also supply strong targets. Higher loss under direct masking likewise does not, by itself, demonstrate optimization instability.

Universal-improvement claims need qualification. In Table A.10, adding MaskSub during finetuning reduces ViT-B CIFAR-100 accuracy from 91.89 to 89.55, well beyond the reported variability. Section 4.2 also states that CLIP finetuning achieves the same best-epoch performance as the baseline; its reported gain therefore concerns final-epoch performance. These are meaningful limits on the plug-in benefit, although the manuscript acknowledges them locally.

Uncertainty reporting is uneven. Repeated runs support the core ViT-S/B experiments, but several smaller gains, including BEiTv2's 0.1-point improvements and downstream detection gains, lack corresponding variability estimates. The GLUE extension also omits task-specific optimization settings and clear evaluation-protocol details, making those auxiliary conclusions less secure than the main vision results.

Some comparative claims are broader than the controls support. Table 6 mixes self-distillation results obtained with substantially different training recipes, although selected matched RSB comparisons help. Efficiency also depends on architecture: ResNet and Swin require approximately twice the training computation because masked regions cannot be removed as tokens.

Minor reporting issues should be separated from the scientific limitations: Table 7 labels both CIFAR columns as CIFAR100, and the statement that all experiments use 50% masking conflicts with the explicitly documented 15% BERT setting. These are readily correctable clarity issues.
